components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early signature tallies and slips were made of bamboo.
佥 (qiān) is an exact match for the sound of 签.
罒 (net) — 署 originally related to an official's net of duties or jurisdiction, giving 'office, bureau.'
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to shǔ's reading, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 两国领导人签署了和平协议。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén qiānshǔle hépíng xiéyì.
example.english: The leaders of the two countries signed a peace agreement.
example.fact: The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648 to end the Thirty Years' War, was actually two treaties signed simultaneously in the German cities of Münster and Osnabrück, because Catholic and Protestant delegates refused to meet in the same room. Historians consider it a founding moment for the modern concept of state sovereignty.

components.note: 犭 (dog) shows 猜 relates to an animal sense used metaphorically for a hunch.
青 (qīng) gives a sound distantly related to cāi, having drifted apart over time.
氵 (water) — 测 originally referred to measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) gives a rhyme close to cè, with the tone and initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 科学家们对恐龙灭绝的原因提出了许多猜测。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen duì kǒnglóng mièjué de yuányīn tíchūle xǔduō cāicè.
example.english: Scientists have proposed many conjectures about the cause of dinosaur extinction.
example.fact: The leading explanation for the dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago is a 10-kilometer-wide asteroid that struck what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, leaving the Chicxulub crater. Geologist Walter Alvarez and his father proposed the theory in 1980 after finding a worldwide layer of iridium-rich clay dating to exactly that time.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

example.hanzi: 相比其他行星，金星的表面温度极高。
example.pinyin: Xiāngbǐ qítā xíngxīng, Jīnxīng de biǎomiàn wēndù jí gāo.
example.english: Compared to other planets, Venus's surface temperature is extremely high.
example.fact: Venus's surface reaches about 465°C, hot enough to melt lead, even though Mercury sits closer to the sun. The cause is a runaway greenhouse effect: a thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide traps heat so effectively that Venus stays hotter than any other planet in the solar system.

components.note: 又 (hand), doubled — two hands side by side depict a pair, giving 双 its meaning 'pair, both, two.'
方 has been read as a pictograph of a plow with a handle, or alternatively of two boats lashed side by side — the original image is debated, but the character came to mean 'square, direction, method.'

example.hanzi: 双方经过长时间谈判终于达成了协议。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng jīngguò cháng shíjiān tánpàn zhōngyú dáchéngle xiéyì.
example.english: Both sides finally reached an agreement after lengthy negotiations.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords between Egypt and Israel were hammered out over 13 tense days at the US presidential retreat in Maryland, mediated personally by President Jimmy Carter. The resulting treaty made Egypt the first Arab nation to formally recognize Israel.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.
里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 科学家精确测量了这批样本的数量。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā jīngquè cèliángle zhè pī yàngběn de shùliàng.
example.english: Scientists precisely measured the quantity of this batch of samples.
example.fact: Avogadro's number, roughly 6.022×10²³, defines the quantity of particles in one mole of any substance — a number so large that one mole of standard sheets of paper stacked up would reach far beyond the width of the observable universe. It's named after Amedeo Avogadro, who never actually calculated the number himself; it was named in his honor decades after his death.

components.note: 罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.
亻 (person) — 伯 names a male relative, a person in the family.
白 (bái) gives the sound — close to bó, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 罗伯特在会议上介绍了新的研究成果。
example.pinyin: Luóbótè zài huìyì shàng jièshàole xīn de yánjiū chéngguǒ.
example.english: Robert presented new research findings at the meeting.
example.fact: English scientist Robert Hooke coined the biological term 'cell' in 1665 after examining a thin slice of cork under a microscope he built himself and noticing tiny box-like compartments that reminded him of monks' rooms, or cells, in a monastery. His book Micrographia was one of the first to popularize the microscopic world.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 对了，你知道长颈鹿的心脏比人的心脏大得多吗？
example.pinyin: Duì le, nǐ zhīdào chángjǐnglù de xīnzàng bǐ rén de xīnzàng dà de duō ma?
example.english: Oh, by the way, did you know a giraffe's heart is much bigger than a human heart?
example.fact: A giraffe's heart can weigh up to 11 kilograms and generates roughly double the blood pressure of most other mammals, which it needs to pump blood all the way up its long neck to the brain, about six meters above the ground. Special valves and tight skin in the legs also prevent blood from pooling when the giraffe lowers its head to drink.

components.note: 匹 pictures a roll of cloth folded over itself — the image behind its meaning 'bolt of cloth,' later extended to a classifier for horses.
酉 (a wine vessel) — 配 originally related to blending or mixing wine
己 (jǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 配's reading pèi, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 这个算法能快速匹配指纹数据库中的记录。
example.pinyin: Zhège suànfǎ néng kuàisù pǐpèi zhǐwén shùjùkù zhōng de jìlù.
example.english: This algorithm can quickly match records in the fingerprint database.
example.fact: Human fingerprints are fully formed by about the seventeenth week of fetal development and stay the same for life outside of scarring, which is why they remain a reliable form of identification. The FBI's fingerprint database, now called the Next Generation Identification system, holds records for well over 100 million people.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — depicts a cave or hole, marking the character as related to a hollow or enclosed space.
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 窒's reading.
自 (nose) — the breath passing through.
心 (heart) — the breath of life, giving 息 its meaning 'to breathe; to rest; news.'

example.hanzi: 潜水员必须小心避免因缺氧而窒息。
example.pinyin: Qiánshuǐyuán bìxū xiǎoxīn bìmiǎn yīn quēyǎng ér zhìxī.
example.english: Divers must be careful to avoid suffocating from lack of oxygen.
example.fact: The human brain can typically survive only about four to six minutes without oxygen before permanent damage begins. Elite free divers train their bodies to trigger the mammalian dive reflex, which slows the heart rate and redirects blood to vital organs, allowing some to hold their breath for over ten minutes underwater.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僵 describes a person's body becoming stiff.
畺 (jiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 僵.
尸 is traditionally read as a picture of a person collapsed or bent over — the origin of its meaning 'corpse.'

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了僵尸入侵城市的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle jiāngshī rùqīn chéngshì de gùshì.
example.english: This movie tells the story of zombies invading a city.
example.fact: In tropical forests, a real fungus called Ophiocordyceps unilateralis infects carpenter ants and hijacks their nervous system, forcing the ant to climb vegetation and clamp its jaws onto a leaf in a spot ideal for the fungus, before a spore-releasing stalk erupts from the dead ant's head. Scientists sometimes call it the 'zombie ant fungus.'

components.note: 豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.
彳 (a step/road) — 征 relates to a long journey or military campaign
正 (zhèng) gives a sound close to 征's reading zhēng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 白鸽常常被视为和平的象征。
example.pinyin: Báigē chángcháng bèi shìwéi hépíng de xiàngzhēng.
example.english: The white dove is often regarded as a symbol of peace.
example.fact: Doves and pigeons are among the very few birds, along with penguins and flamingos, that feed their chicks a nutrient-rich fluid called 'crop milk,' regurgitated from a pouch in their throat rather than food caught in the wild. Both parents produce and share this feeding duty equally.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
亻 (person) shows 仗 relates to a person's action or reliance on something.
丈 (zhàng) gives the exact sound of 仗.

example.hanzi: 古代士兵常常骑马打仗。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài shìbīng chángcháng qímǎ dǎzhàng.
example.english: Ancient soldiers often fought battles on horseback.
example.fact: The stirrup, likely invented in China or Central Asia around the 4th century AD, let mounted soldiers grip their horse securely with their legs and fight with both hands free. Historians credit this simple device with transforming cavalry warfare and helping give rise to the heavily armored knights of medieval Europe.

components.note: 刂 (a knife) — 创 relates to cutting or wounding, extended to mean 'to start, to create,' as a fresh cut marks a new beginning
仓 (cāng) gives a loose sound connection to 创's reading chuàng
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 贝多芬在失聪后仍坚持创作音乐。
example.pinyin: Bèiduōfēn zài shīcōng hòu réng jiānchí chuàngzuò yīnyuè.
example.english: Beethoven continued composing music even after losing his hearing.
example.fact: Beethoven began losing his hearing in his late twenties and was almost completely deaf by the time he composed his Ninth Symphony. He reportedly sawed the legs off a piano and set it on the floor so he could feel the vibrations of the notes through the wood and his own body.

components.note: 片 (a thin slice/board) — 牌 names a flat board or sign, like a nameplate.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pái.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 商店门口挂着一个写着营业中的牌子。
example.pinyin: Shāngdiàn ménkǒu guàzhe yí gè xiězhe yíngyè zhōng de páizi.
example.english: A sign reading 'Open' hangs at the shop's entrance.
example.fact: The Bass Brewery's red triangle logo became the United Kingdom's first officially registered trademark in 1876, the day the new Trade Marks Registration Act took effect, after an employee reportedly camped outside the registry office overnight to be first in line.

components.note: 卫 is the simplified form of 衛, which originally depicted feet moving around a walled settlement — the image of patrolling guards gave rise to its meaning 'to guard, defend,' extended to 'health, hygiene' via the sense of protecting the body.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 医生建议大家勤洗手，注意卫生。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì dàjiā qín xǐshǒu, zhùyì wèishēng.
example.english: Doctors recommend that everyone wash their hands often and pay attention to hygiene.
example.fact: In the 1840s, Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis found that having physicians wash their hands with chlorinated lime before delivering babies cut maternal deaths from childbed fever by nearly 90 percent. His colleagues largely rejected the idea at the time, and it was only decades later, after the acceptance of germ theory, that his work was recognized as a major breakthrough in hygiene.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 这是她的处女作，一经出版就受到广泛好评。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā de chǔnǚzuò, yìjīng chūbǎn jiù shòudào guǎngfàn hǎopíng.
example.english: This is her debut work, and it received widespread praise as soon as it was published.
example.fact: The Virgin Islands were named by Christopher Columbus in 1493 after Saint Ursula and her legendary eleven thousand virgin companions, a story from medieval Christian folklore, apparently because the sheer number of islands and islets he encountered reminded him of the huge legendary retinue.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 图书馆里，大家都小声说话。
example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ, dàjiā dōu xiǎoshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: In the library, everyone speaks in a low voice.
example.fact: The convention of near-total silence in libraries is a fairly modern one, taking hold mostly in the 19th and 20th centuries. The ancient Library of Alexandria, one of the largest libraries of the classical world, is believed to have functioned as a lively center of scholarly debate rather than a hushed reading room.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
散 traditionally depicts a hand (攵) scattering something, like seeds tossed from a basket — the image behind its meaning 'to scatter, disperse.'

example.hanzi: 蒲公英的种子靠风分散到很远的地方。
example.pinyin: Púgōngyīng de zhǒngzi kào fēng fēnsàn dào hěn yuǎn de dìfāng.
example.english: Dandelion seeds are scattered far away by the wind.
example.fact: In 2018, researchers at the University of Edinburgh discovered that each dandelion seed's fluffy tuft creates a stable, ring-shaped vortex of air above it as it falls, a structure never seen before in nature. This 'separated vortex ring' is about four times more efficient at generating drag than a parachute of similar size, letting the tiny seed travel over a kilometer on the wind.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这家博物馆全年向公众开放。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn quánnián xiàng gōngzhòng kāifàng.
example.english: This museum is open to the public all year round.
example.fact: The Louvre in Paris, now the world's most-visited museum, first opened its doors to the public in 1793 during the French Revolution, turning a former royal palace into a place where ordinary citizens, not just nobility, could view its art collection.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 他老是忘记带钥匙。
example.pinyin: Tā lǎoshi wàngjì dài yàoshi.
example.english: He is always forgetting to bring his keys.
example.fact: German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the 'forgetting curve' in 1885 after testing his own memory with nonsense syllables, finding that without any review, people forget roughly half of newly learned information within about an hour and up to 70 percent within a day. His work became a founding study in memory research.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 这座城市正在建设一座大型体育馆。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì zhèngzài jiànshè yí zuò dàxíng tǐyùguǎn.
example.english: This city is building a large-scale stadium.
example.fact: North Korea's Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang is the largest stadium in the world by capacity, seating around 114,000 spectators. It is used mainly for the Arirang Mass Games, a large-scale synchronized gymnastics and artistic performance involving tens of thousands of participants.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 搜 relates to physically searching for something.
叟 (sǒu) gives a sound close to sōu, differing mainly in tone.
彐 (a hand reaching out) — 寻 relates to searching, reaching for something.
寸 (cùn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading xún has diverged.

example.hanzi: 救援队连夜搜寻失踪的登山者。
example.pinyin: Jiùyuánduì liányè sōuxún shīzōng de dēngshānzhě.
example.english: The rescue team searched through the night for the missing climber.
example.fact: The SETI project has used radio telescopes since 1960 to search the sky for signals from other civilizations. Its most famous find, the 1977 'Wow! signal' picked up by Ohio State University's Big Ear telescope, remains an unexplained 72-second burst that has never been detected again.

components.note: 刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 看到这么好笑的视频，她忍不住笑了出来。
example.pinyin: Kàndào zhème hǎoxiào de shìpín, tā rěnbuzhù xiàole chūlái.
example.english: Seeing such a funny video, she couldn't help but laugh.
example.fact: Laughter is famously contagious, a phenomenon linked to mirror neurons that fire both when we act and when we watch someone else act. American sound engineer Charley Douglass exploited this in 1950 by building the 'laff box,' a device used to add pre-recorded laugh tracks to sitcoms, a technique that shaped decades of American television comedy.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.

example.hanzi: 他因为高烧不退，被送去住院观察。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gāoshāo bú tuì, bèi sòng qù zhùyuàn guānchá.
example.english: Because his fever wouldn't go down, he was sent to the hospital for observation.
example.fact: The bimaristans of the medieval Islamic world, some dating to 9th-century Baghdad, are considered among the earliest hospitals with organized wards for different illnesses and rotating medical staff. Patients being discharged were sometimes given a small sum of money to help cover their recovery period.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浴 relates to washing with water.
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound only distantly related to yù today, having drifted apart over time.
缶 (an earthenware vessel) — 缸 names a type of pottery container.
工 (gōng) gives a sound related to 缸's reading gāng, though the final has shifted.

example.hanzi: 她放了满满一浴缸热水，准备泡澡。
example.pinyin: Tā fàngle mǎnmǎn yī yùgāng rè shuǐ, zhǔnbèi pàozǎo.
example.english: She filled the bathtub full of hot water, ready to soak.
example.fact: According to legend, the Greek mathematician Archimedes discovered the principle of buoyancy around 250 BC while stepping into a filled bathtub, noticing the water level rise and realizing an object's volume could be measured by the water it displaced. He supposedly shouted 'Eureka!' and ran through the streets of Syracuse still dripping wet.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后常在球场上打篮球。
example.pinyin: Háizimen fàngxué hòu cháng zài qiúchǎng shàng dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: After school, the children often play basketball on the court.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by Canadian-American physical education instructor James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony at a Massachusetts YMCA to serve as goals. Because the baskets still had their bottoms, someone had to fetch a ladder to retrieve the ball after every single score.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 何 originally depicted a man carrying a load over his shoulder, the root meaning 'to carry,' later borrowed purely for its sound to write the question word 'what, why.'
可 (kě) is close in sound to hé, sharing a similar historical initial and rhyme.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 天气这么好，我们何不去公园散步呢？
example.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème hǎo, wǒmen hébù qù gōngyuán sànbù ne?
example.english: The weather is so nice, why don't we go for a walk in the park?
example.fact: New York's Central Park, designed in 1858 by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux, was entirely man-made and required more blasting powder to remove its rocky terrain than was used at the Battle of Gettysburg five years later. It remains one of the most visited urban parks in the world.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'
口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

example.hanzi: 学校已经告知家长明天放假的消息。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǐjīng gàozhī jiāzhǎng míngtiān fàngjià de xiāoxi.
example.english: The school has already informed parents that there's no class tomorrow.
example.fact: The Pony Express, running from 1860 to 1861 in the United States, relayed messages nearly 2,900 kilometers from Missouri to California in about ten days using riders who swapped horses at stations roughly every 16 kilometers, cutting delivery time from weeks to days before it was made obsolete within two years by the transcontinental telegraph.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 老师指出了这篇作文中的几个错误。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhǐchūle zhè piān zuòwén zhōng de jǐ gè cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher pointed out several mistakes in this essay.
example.fact: In 1912, meteorologist Alfred Wegener pointed out that the coastlines of Africa and South America fit together like puzzle pieces and proposed the theory of continental drift. Most geologists dismissed the idea at the time, and it was not until the 1960s, with the discovery of plate tectonics, that his theory was confirmed.

components.note: 辶 (walk/movement) — 迪 describes moving forward.
由 (a source, a path from) — walking 辶 from a clear starting point 由 gave 迪 its meaning 'to guide, to enlighten.'
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 迪克是我们班上跑得最快的同学。
example.pinyin: Díkè shì wǒmen bān shàng pǎo de zuì kuài de tóngxué.
example.english: Dick is the fastest runner in our class.
example.fact: American high jumper Dick Fosbury revolutionized his sport at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics by going over the bar backwards and headfirst instead of using the traditional straddle technique. His unconventional 'Fosbury Flop' won him a gold medal and is now used by nearly every elite high jumper in the world.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坟 describes a mound of earth, a grave.
文 (wén) gives a sound only distantly related to fén today, having drifted apart over time.
Earth — a grave is dug in the ground.
Gives the sound mò, related to mù but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这座坟墓中发现了许多陪葬品。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhè zuò fénmù zhōng fāxiànle xǔduō péizàngpǐn.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered many burial artifacts in this tomb.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried near the tomb of China's first emperor Qin Shi Huang around 210 BC, contains over 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features. It was discovered entirely by accident in 1974 by farmers digging a well.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 降 originally related to coming down a hill or slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 降's reading jiàng
人 (a person) — the traditional form 臨 pictures someone bending over, as in lying or leaning, to look down.
品 (here representing many items below) — a person leaning over to look down at things below gave 临 its meaning 'to arrive, to be present, to overlook.'

example.hanzi: 夜幕降临，城市的灯光渐渐亮了起来。
example.pinyin: Yèmù jiànglín, chéngshì de dēngguāng jiànjiàn liàngle qǐlái.
example.english: As night fell, the city lights gradually came on.
example.fact: A total solar eclipse creates an eerie sudden darkness called 'totality,' which can drop nearby temperatures several degrees within minutes and confuse animal behavior — birds often fall silent and nocturnal creatures begin to stir. This was well documented across North America during the total eclipse of April 2024.

components.note: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'
日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

example.hanzi: 古埃及是人类历史上最早的文明之一。
example.pinyin: Gǔ Āijí shì rénlèi lìshǐ shàng zuìzǎo de wénmíng zhī yī.
example.english: Ancient Egypt is one of the earliest civilizations in human history.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian civilization thrived along the Nile for more than 3,000 years, and its calendar, based on the river's predictable annual flooding, divided the year into 365 days — a system remarkably close to the calendar most of the world still uses today.

meanings: official (approved or issued by an authority)

components.note: 官 combines 宀 (a roof, building) with a shape traditionally linked to a military garrison or storehouse below it — together depicting an official building, the source of 官's meaning 'official, government.'
方 has been read as a pictograph of a plow with a handle, or alternatively of two boats lashed side by side — the original image is debated, but the character came to mean 'square, direction, method.'

example.hanzi: 政府发布了官方声明，澄清了这一事件。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fābùle guānfāng shēngmíng, chéngqīngle zhè yī shìjiàn.
example.english: The government issued an official statement clarifying the incident.
example.fact: The Behistun Inscription, carved around 500 BC into a cliff in present-day Iran on the order of Persian King Darius I, is one of the oldest known official proclamations, written in three languages. Its trilingual text later became the key that let scholars decipher cuneiform script, much as the Rosetta Stone did for Egyptian hieroglyphs.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 候's meaning 'to wait, time,' as if a person watching and waiting.
矦 (hóu) gives a sound hint — 候 is pronounced hòu, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 三位候选人将在明天的选举中角逐市长职位。
example.pinyin: Sān wèi hòuxuǎnrén jiāng zài míngtiān de xuǎnjǔ zhōng juézhú shìzhǎng zhíwèi.
example.english: Three candidates will compete for the mayoral position in tomorrow's election.
example.fact: Ancient Athens practiced ostracism, in which citizens could vote to exile a person for ten years by scratching their name onto a broken piece of pottery called an ostrakon. Thousands of these inscribed shards have survived, giving historians a direct record of which political candidates and figures were unpopular over 2,400 years ago.

components.note: 夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night
口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 这家夜总会每天晚上都有现场音乐表演。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yèzǒnghuì měitiān wǎnshàng dōu yǒu xiànchǎng yīnyuè biǎoyǎn.
example.english: This nightclub has live music performances every night.
example.fact: Studio 54 in New York City operated for less than a decade, from 1977 to 1986, but became one of the most famous nightclubs in history thanks to its strict door policy and star-studded crowds. Its brief run left a lasting influence on nightlife culture worldwide.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勇 describes inner strength shown as courage.
甬 (yǒng) is an exact match for the sound of 勇.

士 has been read as a pictograph of a battle-axe or as a stylized image of a person standing firm — either way, the shape came to represent a capable man of standing, later broadened to mean 'scholar' or 'soldier.'

example.hanzi: 古代的武士以勇士的精神著称。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài de wǔshì yǐ yǒngshì de jīngshén zhùchēng.
example.english: Ancient warriors were known for their warrior spirit.
example.fact: Japan's samurai followed a code known as bushido, 'the way of the warrior,' which emphasized loyalty, honor, and discipline. The samurai class was formally abolished in 1876 during the Meiji Restoration as Japan replaced its warrior aristocracy with a modern conscript army.

components.note: 牙 pictures two interlocking, jagged shapes — an image of teeth, especially molars, meeting together.
矢 (arrow) — 医 originally related to treating arrow wounds, the root of its meaning 'to cure, doctor'
匸 gives a loose sound connection to 医's reading yī

example.hanzi: 牙医建议我每半年做一次牙齿检查。
example.pinyin: Yáyī jiànyì wǒ měi bàn nián zuò yí cì yáchǐ jiǎnchá.
example.english: The dentist recommended I have a dental checkup every six months.
example.fact: The oldest known dental filling was found in a 13,000-year-old tooth in Italy, where prehistoric people packed a cavity with bitumen mixed with plant fibers and hair. It shows that basic dental care predates written history by thousands of years.

components.note: 三 is made of three simple horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number three, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 二 (two).
十 is thought to depict a knot tied partway along a counting cord, or simply a single vertical mark used to represent a completed count of ten.

example.hanzi: 她今年三十岁，是公司里最年轻的经理。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián sānshí suì, shì gōngsī lǐ zuì niánqīng de jīnglǐ.
example.english: She is thirty years old this year, the youngest manager in the company.
example.fact: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to complete a full cycle of phases, which is close to thirty — a coincidence that led many ancient calendars, including the Babylonian and early Chinese lunar calendars, to build their months around roughly thirty-day cycles.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 棕 names the palm tree, and the brown color associated with its fiber.
宗 (zōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 棕.
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.hanzi: 秋天的树叶渐渐变成了棕色。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè jiànjiàn biànchéngle zōngsè.
example.english: Autumn leaves gradually turned brown.
example.fact: Leaves turn brown, yellow, or orange in autumn because chlorophyll, the green pigment used for photosynthesis, breaks down as daylight shortens. This reveals carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but had been masked by green throughout the summer.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 推 relates to pushing something with the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound connection to 推's reading tuī
氵 (water) — 测 originally referred to measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) gives a rhyme close to cè, with the tone and initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 天文学家推测这颗行星上可能存在液态水。
example.pinyin: Tiānwénxuéjiā tuīcè zhè kē xíngxīng shàng kěnéng cúnzài yètài shuǐ.
example.english: Astronomers speculate that this planet may have liquid water.
example.fact: Europa, one of Jupiter's moons, is thought to hide a liquid water ocean beneath its icy crust that may contain roughly twice the volume of water in all of Earth's oceans combined. That makes it one of the leading candidates in the solar system for finding microbial life beyond Earth.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 审 relates to a formal setting, like a courtroom, where matters are examined
申 (shēn) gives a sound close to 审's reading shěn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.

example.hanzi: 警察对嫌疑人进行了长时间的审问。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá duì xiányírén jìnxíngle cháng shíjiān de shěnwèn.
example.english: The police interrogated the suspect for a long time.
example.fact: The polygraph, popularly known as a 'lie detector,' was developed in the 1920s by American police officer John Larson, but its scientific validity remains disputed. The American Psychological Association notes there is no evidence any single physiological pattern is uniquely tied to lying, which is why most courts do not accept polygraph results as reliable evidence.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舰 names a large military ship.
见 (jiàn) gives the sound — an exact match with 舰.
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.hanzi: 这支舰队将在下周展开一次联合军事演习。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī jiànduì jiāng zài xià zhōu zhǎnkāi yí cì liánhé jūnshì yǎnxí.
example.english: This fleet will conduct a joint military exercise next week.
example.fact: The Spanish Armada of 1588, sent by King Philip II to invade England with about 130 ships, was ultimately defeated by a mix of English naval tactics and a violent storm that scattered the fleet along the coasts of Scotland and Ireland, sinking dozens of vessels.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
⺮ (bamboo) — the material of ancient counting rods.
具 (held in two hands) — bamboo counting rods or an abacus held up for use, the tools of calculation that gave 算 its meaning 'to calculate, count.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.hanzi: 世界上第一台电子计算机诞生于1946年。
example.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng dì yī tái diànzǐ jìsuànjī dànshēng yú yījiǔsìliù nián.
example.english: The world's first electronic computer was born in 1946.
example.fact: ENIAC, completed in 1945 and publicly unveiled in 1946, is often described as the first general-purpose electronic computer. It weighed about 30 tons, filled an entire room, and relied on nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, which failed so frequently that technicians typically had to replace one almost every day.

components.note: The outline pictures a bent, curved container or musical instrument, giving 曲 its meaning 'crooked, bent' and, by extension, 'a tune.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 她哼着一首熟悉的曲子走进了房间。
example.pinyin: Tā hēngzhe yì shǒu shúxī de qǔzi zǒujìnle fángjiān.
example.english: Humming a familiar tune, she walked into the room.
example.fact: The Seikilos Epitaph, a Greek tune carved onto a marble column in what is now Turkey around the 1st or 2nd century AD, is the oldest complete piece of music known to survive from antiquity, preserving both its lyrics and specific melodic notation.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — 实 (simplified from 實) originally depicted a house.
贝 (shell/money, standing in for the traditional 貫, a string of coins) — a house full of valuables gave 实 its meaning 'full, substantial, real.'
方 (here representing a flag or banner, related to 㫃) — 施 originally related to a flag being unfurled and displayed, extended to the idea of carrying out or bestowing something publicly.
也 (yě) is close in sound to shī, sharing a similar historical rhyme though the tone has since shifted.

example.hanzi: 政府将从下个月开始实施新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiāng cóng xià gè yuè kāishǐ shíshī xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government will implement new environmental policies starting next month.
example.fact: The Montreal Protocol, implemented in 1989 to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals such as CFCs, is widely regarded as one of the most successful international environmental treaties ever ratified. The ozone layer over Antarctica has been steadily recovering since, and scientists project it could fully heal by around 2066.

components.note: 舍 (house) — 舒 relates to a sense of settled, at-ease comfort, 'relaxed, comfortable.'
予 (yǔ) is only distantly related in sound to shū — the connection has drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk/move) — 适 relates to fitting well as one moves along, i.e. being suitable
舌 (shé) gives a sound distantly related to 适's reading shì, having drifted apart over a long time

example.hanzi: 这张沙发又软又舒适，坐着看书很惬意。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng shāfā yòu ruǎn yòu shūshì, zuòzhe kànshū hěn qièyì.
example.english: This sofa is soft and comfortable — it's very pleasant to sit and read on it.
example.fact: Memory foam, now common in comfortable mattresses and sofa cushions, was originally developed by NASA in 1966 to cushion astronauts and pilots against the extreme g-forces of spaceflight. It only became widely available in home furniture in the 1990s.

components.note: 冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
讠 (speech) — the act of speaking.
正 (straight, correct) — speaking the straight, correct truth, giving 证 its meaning 'to prove, certify; evidence.'

example.hanzi: 这座古老的桥见证了这座城市数百年的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔlǎo de qiáo jiànzhèngle zhè zuò chéngshì shùbǎi nián de lìshǐ.
example.english: This ancient bridge has witnessed hundreds of years of the city's history.
example.fact: The Charles Bridge in Prague, completed in 1402, has withstood floods, wars, and heavy daily use for over 600 years. A long-standing legend claims egg yolks were mixed into its mortar to strengthen it, though modern chemical analysis has found no clear evidence supporting the story.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.

example.hanzi: 大象是陆地上现存最大的动物。
example.pinyin: Dàxiàng shì lùdì shàng xiàncún zuì dà de dòngwù.
example.english: Elephants are the largest living land animals.
example.fact: African elephants can weigh up to 6,000 kilograms and are among the few animals confirmed to recognize themselves in a mirror, a sign of self-awareness they share with humans, great apes, and dolphins. They also appear to mourn their dead, sometimes returning to visit and touch the bones of deceased herd members.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这个古老的传说讲述了一把拥有魔力的剑。
example.pinyin: Zhège gǔlǎo de chuánshuō jiǎngshùle yì bǎ yǒngyǒu mólì de jiàn.
example.english: This ancient legend tells of a sword with magic power.
example.fact: The legend of Excalibur, King Arthur's magical sword, has roots in Welsh and Breton Celtic mythology. The earliest known written account of a sword given by a supernatural power appears in Geoffrey of Monmouth's 12th-century chronicle Historia Regum Britanniae, long before the more familiar 'Lady of the Lake' version of the story took shape.
